title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: X is a variety over a field K, typically a number field, and Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Γ acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π_1(X) with base points in X(K), or more generally K-rational base points. For a path l : x → y one writes ^u l = g_l(u)·l, or l·f_l(u), with g_l(u) in π̂_1(X,y) and f_l(u) in π̂_1(X,x).

The previous page sets up a van Kampen-type statement. X (its complex or analytic space) is covered by pieces T_α, each simply connected or carrying a distinguished family of paths, with a chain-connectedness condition on overlaps. The elements g^α_{y,x}(u), attached to the canonical 'direct' paths l^α_{y,x} inside T_α (x, y ∈ T_α), then determine the whole Galois action. The reason is that the images of the l^α_{y,x} generate Π_1(X). More precisely, the groupoid presented by these generators, with the compatibility relations φ_{βα} coming from inclusions T_α ⊂ T_β, maps bijectively on π_0 and surjectively on π_1 to Π_1(X).

This page ('6' is a section page number) gives a second proof. Any actual path [0,1] → X decomposes, by a Lebesgue-number argument, into a composite of 'direct' paths x_0 = x → x_1 → … → x_n = y between 'nearby' points, i.e. points lying in a common piece. This settles the case where the interiors of the T_α cover X. When the pieces are closed, a standard descent argument (gluing of covering spaces along a finite closed cover), not needed under the first hypothesis, gives the result.

The advantage of the second proof is a more general, more practical statement. For each α one chooses a subset I_α ⊂ T_α (normally finite), compatible with inclusions: T_α ⊂ T_β implies I_α ⊂ I_β. Typically I ⊂ X(K) is a given set of rational base points, I_α = I ∩ T_α, and I = ∪ I_α. One then restricts to the g^α_{y,x} with x, y ∈ I_α. Their knowledge recovers all g_l(u) for l an arbitrary path between points of I, i.e. the Galois action on the fundamental groupoid π_1(X,I) with base-point set I.

The oblique margin note seems to introduce exactly this π_1(X,I), groupoid with base points in I ⊂ X(k), and the restricted groupoids π_1(T_α, T_α ∩ I).

After the rule: so far X was kept fixed while I, resp. (T/X, x, y), varied. Next one lets u ∈ Γ vary. This leads to the next page's cocycle identities: g_l(uv) = ^u g_l(v)·g_l(u), and f_l(uv) = f_l(u)·^u f_l(v). These say that Γ-torsors and bitorsors are the right language for Π_1(X)^{(x,y)}.

Purpose: reduce the description of the Galois action on a fundamental groupoid (ultimately of Teichmüller/moduli spaces) to finitely many elements attached to the pieces of a decomposition, with base points in each piece.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The closed-cover case tacitly needs a finiteness or local-finiteness hypothesis on the cover (or a triangulability hypothesis) for the descent step and for the decomposition of paths. This is presumably intended ('normalement' finite data) but is not stated.
The surjectivity/bijectivity claims rely on the chain-connectedness condition on overlaps from the previous page; this page does not restate it.

ideas.what: The fundamental groupoid of a space covered by pieces is generated by 'direct' paths within the pieces, modulo the relations from inclusions. Proof: subdivide any path into short paths between nearby points (Lebesgue number); for closed covers use descent.
ideas.modern_name: Van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids (open and closed covers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (1967, 'Groupoids and van Kampen's theorem'; Elements of Modern Topology 1968); Grothendieck SGA1 for the descent version
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX (descent and van Kampen for étale π_1); the groupoid spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid π_1(X,I) based at a chosen set I of (rational) base points, with I_α = I ∩ T_α compatible with inclusions; finite data on the pieces determines the whole groupoid.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid on a set of base points; van Kampen for many base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (1967); Brown–Razak Salleh (1984) for arbitrary covers
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), on fundamental groupoids with base points chosen in each cell; Pursuing Stacks (unsure of the exact passage)

ideas.what: Galois action on the profinite groupoid determined by the elements g^α_{y,x}(u) attached to direct paths in each piece, i.e. by finitely many Galois-theoretic invariants.
ideas.modern_name: Description of G_Q acting on π_1 of moduli spaces via tangential/rational base points and local paths (Ihara–Drinfeld (λ,f) parametrization, GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985–), Drinfeld (1990), Deligne (1989, tangential base points); programmatically Grothendieck, Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2 (Teichmüller tower, groupoids with base points)

ideas.what: Transition to letting u ∈ Γ vary, leading to the 1-cocycle identities for f_l and g_l (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Path torsors as Γ-torsors and bitorsors; Galois cocycles attached to paths

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard van Kampen argument for fundamental groupoids with a chosen set of base points (Brown's framework), applied to reduce the Galois action to data attached to pieces of a decomposition. This idea is visible in Esquisse d'un programme and was developed by Ihara, Drinfeld and Deligne. It is a nice record of Grothendieck's working method, but nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'n tout chemin' is probably '[que] tout chemin' (continuing from the previous page); the '6' at the top is a section page number.
'standard et ignoré dans la première hypothèse' is more plausibly 'standard et inutile dans la première hypothèse'.
'$\mathfrak{J}^\alpha_{y,x}$' should be '$g^\alpha_{y,x}$', the Galois elements of the previous page.
'$\mathfrak{J}_{y,x}(n)$, $x,y$ chemins quelconques dans' is likely '$g_l(u)$, $l$ un chemin quelconque dans [π_1(X,I)]'.
'Dans le cas où les X_α sont fermés' probably refers to the T_α (closed pieces).
